READ-ONLY audit. Do NOT modify/create/delete any file in /opt/nxeon. Do not run builds/migrations/restarts.

Task: audit EVERY file under /opt/nxeon/app/api/**/route.ts for authentication/authorization defects (IDOR, missing auth, admin routes reachable by non-admins, missing rate limits, unbounded data returns, secret leakage in responses).

Method:
1. `find /opt/nxeon/app/api -name route.ts` and read every single one in full.
2. Read /opt/nxeon/lib/auth.ts, /opt/nxeon/lib/rbac.ts, /opt/nxeon/lib/api-auth.ts, /opt/nxeon/lib/rate-limit.ts first so you understand what `requireUser`/`requireAdmin`/`requireArea`/token auth actually enforce (e.g. does requireAdmin throw or return? is the return value checked?).
3. For each route: who can call it, what resource IDs are accepted, is ownership verified against the session user, what is returned (any secrets: rootPassword, totpSecret, anthropicKeyEnc, API tokens, password hashes, session tokens?), is there a `take` limit, is there rate limiting.
4. Pay special attention to: app/api/console/[serverId], app/api/metrics, app/api/track, app/api/log, app/api/health, app/api/admin/export, app/api/account/export, app/api/domains/[id]/dns-export, app/api/claude/[id], app/api/v1/servers, app/api/invoices/[id], app/api/servers/[id]/disk, app/api/search, app/api/stripe/*.

Verify each suspicion by reading the actual code end-to-end. Report only concrete defects with a realistic trigger — no stylistic nits.

Return a findings list. Each finding: severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), absolute file:line, what's wrong, concrete failure scenario (specific request sequence), minimal fix. ALSO explicitly list which routes you checked and found sound. Do not write any report files — return the text directly.

1	import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
2	import type { Role, User } from "@prisma/client";
3	import { realUser } from "./auth";
4	
5	/**
6	 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
7	 *
8	 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
9	 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
10	 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
11	 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
12	 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
13	 */
14	export type Area =
15	  | "overview"
16	  | "analytics"
17	  | "clients"
18	  | "support"
19	  | "fleet"
20	  | "billing"
21	  | "platform";
22	
23	/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
24	export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
25	  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
26	  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
27	  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
28	  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
29	  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
30	  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
31	  platform: ["ADMIN"],
32	};
33	
34	export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
35	  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
36	}
37	
38	/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
39	export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
40	  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
41	}
42	
43	/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */
44	const HREF_AREA: Record<string, Area> = {
45	  "/admin": "overview",
46	  "/admin/analytics": "analytics",
47	  "/admin/users": "clients",
48	  "/admin/support": "support",
49	  "/admin/servers": "fleet",
50	  "/admin/nodes": "fleet",
51	  "/admin/ips": "fleet",
52	  "/admin/provisioning": "fleet",
53	  "/admin/monitoring": "fleet",
54	  "/admin/infrastructure": "fleet",
55	  "/admin/subscriptions": "billing",
56	  "/admin/billing": "billing",
57	  "/admin/invoices": "billing",
58	  "/admin/plans": "billing",

64	  "/admin/testimonials": "platform",
65	  "/admin/feedback": "support",
66	  "/admin/orgs": "clients",
67	  "/admin/visitors": "analytics",
68	  "/admin/logs": "platform",

77	  "/admin/games": "platform",

79	};

81	export function areaForHref(href: string): Area {
82	  return HREF_AREA[href] ?? "platform";
83	}
84	
85	export function canAccessHref(role: Role, href: string): boolean {
86	  return canAccess(role, areaForHref(href));
87	}
88	
89	/**
90	 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
91	 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
92	 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
93	 */
94	export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
95	  const user = await realUser();
96	  if (!user) redirect("/login");
97	  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
98	  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
99	  return user;
100	}

5	/**

7	 *
8	 *   GET /api/account/export  ->  nxeon-data-export.json (attachment)
9	 *
10	 * Strictly scoped to the current user. Secret/credential fields are never
11	 * included: passwordHash, rootPassword, totpSecret, backupCodes, transferEpp
12	 * (domain auth code), anthropicKeyEnc, api-token hashes, Stripe ids.
13	 */
14	export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
15	
16	// Defensive: Prisma BigInt columns (e.g. server bandwidth) aren't JSON-native.
17	function jsonReplacer(_key: string, value: unknown) {
18	  return typeof value === "bigint" ? value.toString() : value;
19	}

24

content.text:
I read all 17 route files in full plus `lib/auth.ts`, `lib/rbac.ts`, `lib/api-auth.ts`, `lib/rate-limit.ts`, `lib/stripe.ts`, `lib/invoices.ts`, `lib/monitoring.ts`, `lib/log.ts`, `lib/proxmox.ts`, `lib/server-metrics.ts`, `lib/actions-tokens.ts`, `lib/order.ts`, `lib/actions-claude.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, and `scripts/console-proxy.mjs`.

## Auth primitive baseline (for context)

- `requireUser`/`requireAdmin`/`requireStaff` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/auth.ts:97-121`) **throw** — but no `route.ts` uses them. Every route does its own inline `currentUser()`/`realUser()` null check and returns a response, and in every case the returned value **is** checked. No "unchecked return" defects.
- `requireArea` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/rbac.ts:94`) calls `redirect()`, which would produce a 307 rather than a 403 in a route handler — but no `route.ts` calls it. `/api/admin/export` correctly uses the non-redirecting `canAccess()` instead.
- `authenticateApiToken` (`/opt/nxeon/lib/api-auth.ts:38`) is sound: sha256 lookup, revoked/expired/suspended all enforced.
- `checkRateLimit` exists and is correct, but **is referenced by exactly one production call site** (`lib/actions.ts:119`, login). Zero API routes rate-limit.

---

# Findings

### 1. CRITICAL — Wallet double-credit via TOCTOU race on unauthenticated confirm endpoint
`/opt/nxeon/app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts:12-19` → `/opt/nxeon/lib/stripe.ts:75-89`

The idempotency guard is a read-then-write with no atomicity and no DB constraint:

```ts
const existing = await db.walletTransaction.findFirst({
  where: { description: { contains: session.id } },
});
if (existing) return false;
await db.$transaction([ db.user.update({ ... increment: cents }), ... ]);
```

`WalletTransaction` (`prisma/schema.prisma:321-328`) has **no unique column** on session id — nothing stops N inserts. The route is unauthenticated, takes `session_id` straight from the query string, and has no rate limit.

**Trigger:** Top up $5 via `/api/stripe/checkout`, pay, land on `/api/stripe/confirm?session_id=cs_live_XXX`. Copy that URL and fire it 20× in parallel (`seq 20 | xargs -P20 -I{} curl -s "https://…/api/stripe/confirm?session_id=cs_live_XXX"`). All 20 handlers are gated on the same ~200 ms `checkout.sessions.retrieve` round-trip, so they all reach `findFirst` before any commits, all see zero rows, and all commit `+500` cents. $5 paid, $100 credited — then spendable on servers via `placeOrder`. If the session carries an order intent, `credited === true` for all 20, so `placeOrder` also runs 20×, provisioning 20 VMs.

This also fires **accidentally**: the Stripe webhook (`/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:21`) calls the same function, and the browser's confirm redirect commonly lands in the same window as the webhook delivery.

**Fix:** add `stripeSessionId String? @unique` to `WalletTransaction`, write it inside the same `$transaction`, and treat a `P2002` unique violation as "already credited → return false". (Bonus: removes the unindexed `LIKE '%cs_...%'` full-table scan that currently widens the race window as the table grows.)

---

### 2. HIGH — `/api/log` is an unauthenticated outbound-webhook amplifier and request-blocking sink
`/opt/nxeon/app/api/log/route.ts:8-26` → `/opt/nxeon/lib/log.ts:26-38`

No auth, no origin check, no rate limit. The handler `await`s `logError`, which `await`s a `fetch` to `NXEON_ERROR_WEBHOOK` with a 3 s timeout, embedding attacker-controlled `context` (80 chars), `message` (500), `path` (200) and `stack` (2000) verbatim in the alert body.

**Trigger:** `while :; do curl -sX POST https://nxeon/api/log -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"context":"DB CREDENTIALS LEAKED","message":"<attacker text>","stack":"…2000 chars…"}' & done`. Two effects: (a) the ops alert channel is flooded with forged, attacker-authored "🚨 Nxeon …" alerts — an incident-response poisoning / social-engineering primitive; (b) each request pins a Node request slot for up to 3 s awaiting the webhook, so a few hundred concurrent requests saturate the app server. Also unbounded journald growth.

**Fix:** `checkRateLimit(\`log:${clientIp}\`, { max: 20, windowMs: 60_000 })` at the top of the handler, and make the webhook fan-out fire-and-forget (drop the `await` on `logEvent`, or only forward to the webhook when `source !== "client"`).

---

### 3. HIGH — `/api/track` allows unauthenticated unbounded row insertion
`/opt/nxeon/app/api/track/route.ts:26-59`

No auth, no rate limit, no per-IP cap. Every non-bot POST unconditionally does `db.visit.create({...})` with a 300-char `path`, 400-char `referrer`, 400-char `ua`.

**Trigger:** `for i in $(seq 1 500000); do curl -sX POST 'https://nxeon/api/track?k=portal' -H 'user-agent: Mozilla/5.0' -d '{"path":"/'$i'","referrer":"https://evil/'$(head -c400 /dev/urandom|base64)'"}' & done` — roughly 1 KB of durable DB storage per request, from an unauthenticated client. Fills the Postgres volume (which also hosts VM billing state), and poisons `/admin/visitors` and `/admin/analytics` with fabricated traffic. The `x-forwarded-for` guard doesn't help: the attacker just spoofs a different first hop per request, defeating any naive per-IP grouping too.

**Fix:** rate-limit on `clientIp(req)` (e.g. `max: 60, windowMs: 60_000`) before the `create`, and reject requests whose `x-forwarded-for` first hop isn't present (nginx always sets it).

---

### 4. MEDIUM — `/api/metrics` queries the wrong Proxmox node → cross-tenant metrics disclosure
`/opt/nxeon/app/api/metrics/route.ts:21` → `/opt/nxeon/lib/proxmox.ts:151-153`

```ts
const data = await vmRrd(server.vmid, timeframe);   // vmRrd → pve.get(`/nodes/${NODE}/qemu/${vmid}/rrddata`)
```

`vmRrd` always uses the env-configured **primary** node and the primary credentials, ignoring `server.node`. The sibling disk route gets this right — `/opt/nxeon/app/api/servers/[id]/disk/route.ts:26-34` builds a `NodeConn` from `server.node` and `serverDiskRrd` uses `pveFor(conn)` (`lib/server-metrics.ts:26-31`).

Vmids are allocated per-cluster via `/cluster/nextid` (`lib/proxmox.ts:108-110`, `133-136`), so two servers on two *standalone* `Node` rows (distinct `apiUrl`) collide on vmid by design.

**Trigger:** Attacker owns server A on secondary node `pve-de1` with `vmid=104`. Some other customer's server B on the primary node also has `vmid=104`. `GET /api/metrics?serverId=<A>&tf=week` passes the ownership check on A, then reads RRD data for **B** — CPU/RAM/network/disk-IO time series for a server the caller doesn't own. Silent: the caller gets a plausible-looking chart with no error.

**Fix:** give `vmRrd` an optional `conn?: NodeConn` parameter mirroring `serverDiskRrd`, and pass `server.node` from the route (the route already needs `include: { node: true }` added to its `findUnique`).

---

### 5. MEDIUM — `/api/console/[serverId]` has no rate limit; any tenant can exhaust hypervisor resources
`/opt/nxeon/app/api/console/[serverId]/route.ts:41-104`

Each GET issues `POST /nodes/{node}/qemu/{vmid}/vncproxy?websocket=1` on the Proxmox node. Proxmox spawns a `vncproxy` helper process bound to an ephemeral port that lingers until connected or timed out. The route has ownership checks but no throttle and no cap on outstanding tickets.

**Trigger:** Sign up, deploy the cheapest (or a free) VPS, wait for `RUNNING`, then `while :; do curl -s -b "$COOKIE" https://nxeon/api/console/$SID >/dev/null & done`. At a few hundred requests/second the node accumulates thousands of orphaned vncproxy processes and held ports, degrading or wedging the hypervisor — affecting **every** tenant on that node, not just the attacker.

**Fix:** `checkRateLimit(\`console:${user.id}\`, { max: 10, windowMs: 60_000 })` immediately after the ownership check, returning 429 with `Retry-After`.

---

### 6. MEDIUM — API token `scopes` are resolved but never enforced
`/opt/nxeon/app/api/v1/servers/route.ts:14-23`

`authenticateApiToken` returns `scopes` (`lib/api-auth.ts:65`) and the route destructures `auth` but never inspects `auth.scopes`. Tokens are created with `["read"]` or `["write"]` (`lib/actions-tokens.ts:16,27-31`) and the UI presents these as a meaningful restriction.

**Trigger:** Create a token in `/dashboard/settings` selecting only the `write` checkbox. `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer nxe_…" https://nxeon/api/v1/servers` returns the full server list (ids, names, statuses, IPs) despite the token never being granted read. Impact is currently bounded because `/api/v1` has exactly one read-only endpoint — but the scope model is decorative, so any future `/api/v1` write route inherits the same gap.

**Fix:** add a shared `requireScope(auth, "read")` helper in `lib/api-auth.ts` and call it in every `/api/v1` route; return 403 `insufficient_scope` on mismatch.

---

### 7. LOW — `/api/health` leaks internal error text to unauthenticated callers
`/opt/nxeon/app/api/health/route.ts:32-37`, and `/opt/nxeon/lib/monitoring.ts:300-302`

`dbHealth()` returns `String(e?.message ?? e).slice(0, 120)` as the public `db.detail`, and the route's own catch returns `detail: String(e?.message ?? e).slice(0, 160)`. The route is explicitly unauthenticated and documented "no secrets".

**Trigger:** Take Postgres down or point it at a bad host; `curl https://nxeon/api/health` returns a 503 whose body contains the raw driver error — typically `connect ECONNREFUSED 10.x.x.x:5432` or `password authentication failed for user "nxeon"`, disclosing the internal DB host, port and username to anyone polling the status endpoint.

**Fix:** log the message via `logError` and return a fixed string (`detail: "unreachable"`) in the public body.

---

### 8. LOW — `/api/domains/[id]/dns-export` and `/api/domains/check` relay upstream registrar errors, and neither is throttled
`/opt/nxeon/app/api/domains/[id]/dns-export/route.ts:36-39`; `/opt/nxeon/app/api/domains/check/route.ts:26-28`

Both echo `String(e.message).slice(0, 200)` from the registrar client back to the caller, which can surface upstream API endpoints, account identifiers, or quota messages. Separately, `/api/domains/check` performs up to 8 upstream availability lookups per request (`route.ts:21`) with no rate limit — any signed-up user can loop it (`while :; do curl -b "$COOKIE" 'https://nxeon/api/domains/check?q=a'$RANDOM; done`) to burn the platform's registrar API quota or trip an upstream ban affecting all customers.

**Fix:** return a generic message and log the detail; add `checkRateLimit(\`domcheck:${user.id}\`, { max: 20, windowMs: 60_000 })`.

---

### 9. LOW — `/api/admin/export` returns the entire table with no `take` or streaming
`/opt/nxeon/app/api/admin/export/route.ts:58-67` and `:106-110`

Authorization is correct (see below), but `db.user.findMany` with the `servers` relation included, and `db.invoice.findMany`, both materialize every matching row plus the assembled CSV string in memory. With `?q=` empty this is the whole user base. At scale a single SUPPORT operator clicking "Export CSV" can OOM the Node process — a self-inflicted availability event rather than an access-control one.

**Fix:** paginate with a cursor loop and stream the CSV via a `ReadableStream` response, or cap with `take: 50_000`.

---

### 10. LOW — Console relay defaults to plaintext `ws://`
`/opt/nxeon/app/api/console/[serverId]/route.ts:132-136`

When `CONSOLE_PUBLIC_WS_URL` is unset the route hands the browser `ws://${PUBLIC_IP}:8899/console?sid=<JWE>`. The JWE correctly protects the Proxmox token secret and VNC ticket, and the relay enforces single-use jti + 60 s expiry (`scripts/console-proxy.mjs:332-336`), so credential theft is not the issue — but the **VNC session itself** (root console framebuffer and keystrokes) then crosses the public internet unencrypted. Any on-path observer watches an admin type into a customer's root shell.

**Fix:** refuse to issue a ticket when `NODE_ENV === "production"` and `CONSOLE_PUBLIC_WS_URL` does not start with `wss://`, returning the existing 500 `console not configured`.

---

## Routes checked and found sound

- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/account/export/route.ts`** — `currentUser()` checked; every query hard-scoped to `where: { userId: user.id }`; `select` allowlists exclude `passwordHash`, `rootPassword`, `totpSecret`, `backupCodes`, `transferEpp`, `anthropicKeyEnc`, `stripeCustomerId`. BigInt replacer present. No ID is accepted from the client, so no IDOR surface. Sound.
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/admin/export/route.ts`** (authorization only) — correctly uses `realUser()` rather than `currentUser()`, so an impersonating admin can't be tricked into exporting under a customer identity; gates `type=users` on `canAccess(role, "clients")` and `type=invoices` on `canAccess(role, "billing")`. `CUSTOMER` fails both (`lib/rbac.ts:24-36`). `status` is validated against an allowlist; `q` goes through Prisma's parameterized `contains`. CSV cells are escaped (`:19-22`). Authorization is sound (see #9 for the unrelated memory issue).
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/claude/[id]/route.ts`** — `select` fetches `userId` and enforces `build.userId !== user.id && role !== "ADMIN"` → 404 (not 403, so no existence oracle). Returns only `status`/`steps`/`log`/`plan`, all owner-scoped build output; the Anthropic key is never read here (it lives in `lib/actions-claude.ts:45` and is only decrypted worker-side). `no-store`. Sound.
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/console/[serverId]/route.ts`** (authz only) — owner-or-ADMIN enforced at `:54`, 404 on failure; SUPPORT/BILLING correctly excluded; the response contains only `{ wsPath, ticketId }` with the Proxmox `tokenId`/`tokenSecret`/`vncticket` sealed in an A256GCM JWE keyed off `sha256("nxeon-console:" + AUTH_SECRET)`, 60 s expiry, single-use jti verified by the relay. Authorization and secret handling are sound (see #5, #10).
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/domains/[id]/dns-export/route.ts`** (authz only) — owner-or-ADMIN enforced at `:21`; CSV values escaped at `:42`; filename derived from a registrar-validated domain name. Sound apart from #8.
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/invoices/[id]/route.ts`** — owner-or-ADMIN enforced at `:25-29`. I specifically checked `renderInvoiceHTML` for stored XSS since it serves `text/html` on the app origin and an admin views customer-controlled data: `user.name`, `user.email`, `invoice.description`, `period`, and every line-item `description`/`qty` all pass through `esc()` (`lib/invoices.ts:96-102`), which escapes `& < > "`. Numeric fields go through `money()`. No injection point. `private, no-store`. Sound.
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/search/route.ts`** — non-admin queries all carry `userId: user.id`; the user-table branch is ADMIN-gated at `:52`. Every query has an explicit `take` (6/4/4/5) plus a final `slice(0, 15)`. `include: { user: true }` at `:19` pulls full user rows into memory including `passwordHash`, but the response is built from an explicit allowlist (`type`/`label`/`sub`/`href`) and `s.user.email` is only read when `isAdmin` — nothing leaks. `q` is parameterized. Sound.
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/servers/[id]/disk/route.ts`** — owner-or-ADMIN at `:20` → 404; correctly passes the per-node `NodeConn` (the thing `/api/metrics` gets wrong); `tf` is unvalidated in the route but allowlisted inside `serverDiskRrd` (`lib/server-metrics.ts:24`) before reaching Proxmox. Returns only the time series plus the plan's disk size. Sound.
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/metrics/route.ts`** (authz only) — `tf` allowlisted at `:10`; ownership enforced at `:18` → 404; the node-wide RRD branch is ADMIN-gated at `:24`. Authorization is sound; the node-routing bug is #4.
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/stripe/checkout/route.ts`** — authenticated; amount coerced with `Number.isFinite` and bounded $5–$5000 (so no negative or NaN amounts); `customer_email` and `metadata.nxeonUserId` come from the session user, never from the body, so a caller cannot direct the credit at another account; `success_url`/`cancel_url` are built from `APP_URL`, not from input — no open redirect. Sound.
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts`** — requires `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, requires the `stripe-signature` header, and verifies via `constructEvent` on the **raw** body before touching anything; only handles `checkout.session.completed`. Signature verification is correct. (It shares the racy `creditCheckoutSession` from #1, but the webhook path itself is properly authenticated.)
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/v1/servers/route.ts`** (authn only) — bearer auth is correct and `where: { userId: auth.user.id }` is hard-scoped; the `select` returns only id/name/status/ip — no `rootPassword`, no token material. Scope enforcement is the gap (#6).
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/health/route.ts`** (structure) — genuinely intended to be public; 15 s in-process cache prevents DB/Proxmox hammering; the report shape carries no per-customer data. Only the error-detail passthrough (#7) is a problem.
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/track/route.ts`** (input handling) — correctly refuses to trust a body-supplied IP, reads only the first `x-forwarded-for` hop, clips all strings, and drops same-origin referrers. The gap is purely the missing throttle (#3).
